intro: Belgium is split between Dutch-speaking Flanders and French-speaking Wallonia, with a small German-speaking community and a very international capital.

chapters.title: Three languages
text: About six in ten Belgians speak Dutch, often called Flemish, in the north; most of the rest speak French, in the south. A small German-speaking community lives in the east. Brussels is officially bilingual, though mostly French-speaking.
Brussels is one of Europe's most diverse cities, with many residents from Morocco, Turkey, Congo and other EU countries.

chapters.title: Belgian life
text: Belgium's main cities include Brussels, Antwerp, Ghent, Charleroi and Liège. Most Belgians are Catholic by tradition, and voting in elections is compulsory.
